history.summary: CSV ERROR / DUPLICATE FLAG: no documented 'Siddheshwar Dham' exists in Soreng district - every reference found is to Siddheshwar Dham (Solophok Chardham) on Solophok Hill, ~5 km from NAMCHI in Namchi district. This row should be corrected to Namchi or dropped as a duplicate of the Namchi entry. Documented here with the corrected location. Siddheshwar Dham is a Hindu pilgrimage-cum-tourism complex built by the Sikkim government (Rs 56+ crore, 29 ha), inaugurated 8 November 2011. Its centrepiece is a 108-ft seated Lord Shiva statue encircled by replicas of the 12 Jyotirlingas and the four Char Dham temples (Badrinath, Jagannath, Dwarka, Rameshwaram), plus an 18-ft Kirateshwar statue, Nandi, and a Sai Baba temple. Legend links Solophok Hill to Arjuna's tapasya before receiving the Pashupata weapon - the same Kirateshwar tradition as Legship (see 916).

town_description: Solophok Hill rises ~5 km from Namchi town in Namchi district, South Sikkim, with sweeping views of the Kanchenjunga range. Namchi is a major religious-tourism hub (also home to the 135-ft Guru Padmasambhava statue at Samdruptse and the Sai Mandir at Temi); the Chardham complex is its flagship attraction.
